instrument: THE THREE BLOCKERS, FIXED AND MEASURED — and the mechanism, once working, DEGRADES the lane

1_extraction.what: `indexTree` has always accepted a `fileName` parameter and NEVER USED IT, while BOTH callers omitted it — and the SCSS spec's own comment said the module name 'is the file's basename (handled by the caller via file path)'. Added `DeclarationSpec.nameFromFile`, made the type branch fall back to the file's basename when the resolved name is empty and the spec opts in, passed the path at both call sites, and set `nameFromFile: true` in the SCSS spec. Absent the flag every other language reads byte-for-byte what it read.
1_extraction.acceptance: `typeMembers['functions.scss'] size: 12` and `symbolNames` now carries `functions.scss`, `bulmaStringToNumber`, `bulmaEnoughContrast`, … — it was `[]` before. THE LEAD'S ACCEPTANCE TEST MET: non-empty for the 12-function file.

2_serialization.what: `__closedMembers` was attached at runtime (`:983`) and NOT carried by `SerializedProjectIndex`, so every deserialized index — the worker's and the gate's — had it `undefined` and `resolveModuleImports` returned at its first guard. Added the field to the payload and the rebuild on deserialize, AND made `serializeProjectIndex` attach it via `buildResolutionTables` when absent: the indexer's path (`buildProjectIndexFromDisk` -> serialize) never called that, so fixing the payload alone would have carried an empty map.
2_serialization.acceptance: round-tripped `__closedMembers present? true`, size 3, `functions.scss -> [bulmaStringToNumber, bulmaEnoughContrast, bulmaColorBrightness, …]`.
2_serialization.andTheInstrument: `roundTripProjectIndex` checked every DECLARED field and this one is attached at runtime, so the transport test passed while the field was lost. It now checks `__closedMembers` too — a test that enumerates the fields it knows about cannot see a field nobody declared.

3_matching.what: the resolver matched `@use` SPECIFIERS against index type names with `typeName.endsWith('/' + modulePath)`. A specifier is a path and the index names a module by its basename. Now matched by basename with Sass conventions normalised on BOTH sides (leading `_`, `.scss/.sass/.css`), reading `typeMembers` (declared) with `__closedMembers` (inherited) on top, and the emitted edge carries the import statement's own line instead of a fabricated `0`.
3_matching.count: over the whole corpus, of **225** namespaced `@use`/`@forward` specifiers: **the old rule reached 0 · the new rule reaches 123**. (8 repos' indexes still come back empty — a residual gap, stated rather than hidden.)

theMechanismNowWorksAndItsEffectIsNegati.reading: the mechanism emits **+3,206 `exports` edges, of which +3,182 are AMBIGUOUS** — the lane's residual rises 2,566 -> 5,748. It does not add resolved edges: resolved 20,567 -> 20,591 (+24). THE CAUSE IS THE QUALIFIED NAME: every importing file emits `ns.member` (e.g. `cv.bulmaStringToNumber`) and pushes a symbol of that name, so a module imported by N files produces N declarations of the same name and the gate reads them as collisions.
theMechanismNowWorksAndItsEffectIsNegati.nextFixShape: the delegate already has the mechanism for exactly this — `publishFileScopedIdentities` gives same-named symbols file-scoped qualified names (`file::name`, `file#2::name`). The emitted member symbols/edges need the same treatment on the edge side, or the resolver should not emit per-file member edges at all.

regressionDetector.extOK: **6,841 -> 6,841, UNCHANGED** — the Lead's stop condition was not triggered. imports extOK 3,108 and references extOK 3,733 are individually unchanged too.

cssControl.verdict: 0 of 6 columns differ (exit 0) — the verified neighbour is unmoved by all three fixes.

otherColumns: references, imports, extends, calls, overrides, uses, contains: ALL IDENTICAL between the before and after arms. Only `exports` moved.

gates.cmd: npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts scss scss 0 --index (after the fixes)
npx tsx script/m14/residual-gate.ts --lane css (after the fixes)
